atoms.b: Starting from around AD 200, the Romans began experiencing attacks across many other parts of the empire. Many ((++soldiers priests)) stationed in Roman Britain were moved to defend key areas.

From AD 235, Rome also faced a leadership crisis with 20 different ((++emperors chieftains)) ruling in less than 50 years. Some generals brought their ((++armies tribes)) back to Rome to compete for power, including soldiers from Britain.

feedback.finish: With more and more soldiers being recalled from Britain, nearby tribes saw an opportunity to attack.

atoms.a: The Picts were a group of people who lived in Scotland.
The Saxons were from northern Germany and Denmark.

feedback.finish: From around AD 250, with the leadership crisis weakening Roman control, these tribes began to raid Britain more frequently, attacking both Roman forts and local Britons.

trainers.instruction: Listen and select the correct answer.

atoms.a: Why did raiders attack poor farmers?

b.sound: They wanted to steal their livestock.
They wanted to steal their jewels.

atoms.a: Why did raiders attack Roman forts?

b.sound: They wanted to steal weapons for their own warriors.
They wanted to move in and live under Roman rule.

atoms.a: Why did raiders attack wealthy people?

b.sound: They wanted to steal coins, jewels and valuable religious relics.
They wanted to steal their crops and farming tools.

atoms.text: The Romans knew that most of the raiders were coming by sea, so they started to build more forts by the coast and along large rivers to stop them.
The strongest raids came from the Saxons, who were mainly landing in the south-east of Britain. This became the area that was most important to defend.

atoms.a: Why did the Romans build forts on the coast?
b: building materials were easier to find there

atoms.a: Where in Britain did the Romans build more forts to defend against the Saxons?

trainers.instruction: Drag the fort to the correct location to defend against the Saxons.

feedback.correct: Many Roman ruins can still be found in the south-east of England. The forts connected to form a defensive network known as the Saxon Shore.

feedback.wrong: This area was already fortified by Hadrian’s Wall thanks to Roman clashes with the Picts in previous centuries.
While some Roman forts were built in this area, they were primarily there to defend against the Scots.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: This is the site of a Roman fort on the East Kent coast known as Regulbium. The site had existed since the Roman conquest, but as raids became more common, it was expanded with new stone walls to defend against the Saxons.
atoms.sound: This is the site of a Roman fort on the East Kent coast known as Rehgoollbium. The site had existed since the Roman conquest, but as raids became more common, it was expanded with new stone walls to defend against the Saxons.

atoms.text: Many of the soldiers stationed at Regulbium had previously served at Hadrian’s Wall in the far north of Roman Britain. They built the fort in the style of the defences they had seen there while defending against the Picts.
atoms.sound: Many of the soldiers stationed at Rehgoollbium had previously served at Hadrian’s Wall in the far north of Roman Britain. They built the fort in the style of the defences they had seen there while defending against the Picts.

atoms.a: Why did the Romans decide to strengthen Regulbium with stone walls?
atoms.sound: Why did the Romans decide to strengthen Rehgoollbium with stone walls?
b: to house more soldiers being sent to Britain
to provide a safe place for merchants
the efficiency of the Roman roads
the local customs used by Saxon villages

feedback.finish: Many forts were built and strengthened, but the empire still needed soldiers elsewhere. Too few remained to defend the forts properly, so the raids continued.
